newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Olympian Steve Brimacombe won the mens 100 metre final at the Optus Grand Prix in Sydney last night. A 12,000 strong crowd came to see American athlete Carl Lewis compete in a farewell appearance. Lewis finished seventh and took a lap of honour after the race. Page 16.

Western Australia defeated Tasmania in their Sheffield Shield cricket match at Bellerive Oval in Hobart, Tasmania, yesterday to become favourites for Shield champions. Western Australia won by seven wickets in a rain delayed match to take an outright leadon the Shield table. Page 16.

Australian Rugby Union may mediate in a contract dispute between two states over winger Damian Smith. Smith, who is contracted to play for Queensland has joined the New South Wales squad in training. The Queensland Rugby Union claims to have the legal high ground in the dispute that may see Smith sit out from the game for up to two seasons.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian touring car driver Jim Richards has accepted a full time deal with Volvo for 1997. Richards takes over from Peter Brock who held an impressive record of five Bathurst 1000 wins and successes in the NASCAR series. Page 39.

Soccer Australia has reviewed wages for players and refused demands from the players' union for payment of 75 percent of prize money from games to players. Soccer Australia may have offered a compromise of between 50 and 60 percent of prize money to players, an have told players to accept or miss out on World Cup Qualifiers. Page 39.

Greg Blewett became the 16th Australian batsman to be dismissed for 99 in the fourth test match against the West Indies at Adelaide yesterday. Blewett, playing in front of a home crowd, was bowled by West Indian Cameron Cuffy but still received an ovationfrom the crowd. Page 41.
THE AGE

Australia is close to beating the West Indies and winning the Frank Warrell trophy as play begins in day four of the cricket test match in Adelaide today. Australia leads by 234 runs with the West Indies at six for 154. Australia was bowled out on day thre for 517 runs with an overall first innings lead of 387. Page C6.

Changes to the tennis balls and sponsorship names are likely to made to next year's Ford Australian Open. Harder and faster balls may be used in response to player complaints about the balls used at this year's Open, and the name of major sponsor Ford maybe dropped from the title of the event. Page C5.

Victoria is set to produce some of the best surfers in Australia and internationally as competitors prepare to take on the World Qualifying Series this weekend in the Sunshine Pro on the Sunshine Coast in Queensland. Victorian's Glyndyn Ringrose and Troy Brooks will compete in the event. Page C4.
THE HERALD SUN

Six Australian Football League clubs may abstain from participating in next month's pre-season draft of players due to a lack of talented players. Clubs unlikely to participate are Fremantle, Geelong and Adelaide. Page 70.

Australian Olympic soccer captain Kevin Muscat was cautioned for an over-the-top tackle in an FA cup match for his club Crystal Palace against Leeds United. The tackle left Leeds player Lee Boyer with a severe ankle injury in the match that Leeds won 1-0. Page 66.

Australian cycling stars Deane Rogers and Nathan O'Neill will miss the Tour of Tasmania with injuries. Rogers has three fractured vertebrae from a fall in the Bay Classic at Portarlington while O'Neill stabbed himself in the right leg with his brake lever at his Gold Coast home. The Tour of Tasmania starts with a 128 km stage from Devonport today. Page 62.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian runner Melinda Gainsford Taylor was defeated in her 200 metre race by Victorian junior Lauren Hewitt in Sydney last night. It was an upset defeat for Gainsford-Taylor, who is Australia's premier 200 metre runner. Page 52.

Australian Olympic silver medallist Cathy Freeman won her 400 metre race at the Optus Grand Prix in Homebush by nearly a full second from her nearest rival. Freeman is the only Australian to run under 50 seconds for the 400 metre event. Page 52.

Horse trainer Gai Waterhouse has withdrawn Australia's only starter in the Dubai World Cup next month. Waterhouse withdrew Juggler from the A$5.5 million cup to concentrate on preparation for the Sydney autumn carnival. Page 55.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
